tasks.short: Test geological samples, calculate fixed results and document the supported interpretation.

steps.what: Verify sample identity and prepare the apparatus and testing method
Test the samples and observe their content and characteristics
Record sample readings, units, preparation factors and test quality observations
Calculate sample results using the fixed testing formulas
Analyze the results and determine supported sample content and characteristics
Write the sample analysis findings and their limitations

tasks.design: Configure native sample fields and findings headings in {OTHER}, the laboratory records system, and fixed validated calculations in {SPREADSHEET}. Keep preparation, physical testing and interpretation with the technician; separately capture readings, calculate results and write the analysis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sample readings, preparation factors and standard calculations are repeatedly entered and worked through.
tasks.enabler_now: Native sample records and fixed formulas can support consistent result preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Contamination, sample condition and anomalous responses affect validity and interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the apparent result is not a trustworthy sample characteristic.

ambition.what: Notice missing preparation context before interpreting sample results.

tasks.altitude: Focus analysis effort on validity rather than repeated calculation.

reach.learn: Check method, preparation and uncertainty before comparison.

evidence.claim: SampleManager LIMS tracks samples, test assignments and changes; this supports native sample record capability rather than autonomous geological interpretation.
Fixed method formulas and native findings templates could reduce calculation and documentation effort; this task saving is E1.

assumptions: OTHER means the laboratory records system. Existing test equipment operation is fully retained; no new gain is attributed to its inherent measurement function.

The technician produces sample ID, method, reading, units, preparation factor and quality observations in s3, retaining eight hours. Missing factors or suspect measurements stop calculation and require manual correction or retesting.
The formula owner provides the validated method formulas; checking them against the actual sample method is included in setup. No automated interpretation or release is proposed.
Native fields and formulas come first. Same-system author saves have no added approval stage or separate saving.
unknowns: Existing formula automation and sample preparation variation.
research_questions: Do fixed calculations save work after preparation-factor checks and anomalous samples are handled?

already_counted.description: Capture test readings and preparation context.

incremental.description: Maintain and verify formulas and native sample fields.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=86, gross=14; upkeep=4 gives net=10. Conservative case: unusual preparation factors retain five of ten calculation hours and all record and prose work, R=95, net=1. Where formulas fit, two calculation hours plus nine reading-entry and nine findings-writing hours remain, R=90, net=6. Preparation, physical tests and interpretation retain 70 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile testing and operational records into a checked dataset for further analysis.

steps.what: Gather the relevant testing and operational data with their source references
Digitise source values and record identity, units and field mappings
Convert source field names, codes and units to the analysis schema
Compile and log the standardised rows in a draft analysis file
Check compiled data against source records and resolve gaps or mismatches
Load the checked final dataset into the separate analysis repository

tasks.design: Use fixed mappings and a native compilation layout in {SPREADSHEET}, drawing on original records in {OTHER}, the laboratory records system, and {DOCS}. After human source reconciliation, load the exact checked file into {DATA_PLATFORM}, the separate analysis repository, replacing real second-system re-keying.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source records require repeated coding, compilation and entry into the analysis repository.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable field mappings and supported file imports can replace repeated transformations.
tasks.still_hard: Missing identities, mixed units and inconsistent test or operational contexts need manual resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Determine whether records can be combined without misrepresenting their meaning.

ambition.what: Identify inconsistent source coverage before scientific analysis.

tasks.altitude: Move compilation effort toward source comparability and provenance.

reach.learn: Inspect source coverage, transformations and unresolved gaps.

evidence.claim: Fixed mappings, native compilation views and repository imports could replace repeated data transformation and re-keying; this is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: OTHER means the laboratory records system. Original sample test entries are produced in the testing task and are not credited twice; this task owns cross-record compilation into a second analysis repository.

The technician produces source rows, sample or operation ID, time, units, method and target field mapping in s2 with all 20 hours retained, including manual digitisation from paper. Missing identities or unmappable units stop conversion and require manual correction.
Native mappings and imports come first. The final repository load is a real cross-system action, separately priced and gated on the checked file; an ordinary author save receives no gate or saving.
The source producer's measurement work is existing input production, and locating and verifying those records is counted in s1 and s5.
unknowns: Record comparability and repository import support.
research_questions: What manual transformation remains when old units and sample identifiers cannot be mapped reliably?

already_counted.description: Digitise source records and capture field mappings.

incremental.description: Maintain mappings, repository imports and exception handling.

approvals.approved_version: Exact checked file, source row set, units, mappings and target analysis repository; any change requires renewed s5 reconciliation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=52, gross=48; upkeep=8 gives net=40. Conservative case: incompatible legacy codes retain 15 collection, 20 digitisation, 17 conversion, ten compilation, 20 checks and five manual load hours, R=87, net=5. Comparable modern records retain 12 collection, 20 digitisation, ten conversion, zero compilation, 20 checks and five load hours, R=67, net=25.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare geological notes, sketches, maps and cross-sections with traceable interpretation.

steps.what: Retrieve geological observations, borehole records and relevant base map layers
Determine the map or cross-section purpose, extent and appropriate source coverage
Record source coordinates, depths, units and geological observation attributes
Prepare notes, sketches, map geometry or section traces using native drawing tools
Interpret geological relationships and annotate the drawing's uncertainty and evidence limits
Populate the geological output layout with scale, legend and source references
Check the geological maps, sections or notes against their sources and interpretation

tasks.design: Configure source views, drawing presets and output layouts in {OTHER}, the geological mapping and drafting system, with linked records in {DOCS}. Retain scope, input capture, geological interpretation and source checks; simplify native drawing work and give layout population its own step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source attributes, drawing conventions and output metadata are repeatedly organised.
tasks.enabler_now: Native drawing presets and layouts can reuse explicitly captured geological attributes.
tasks.still_hard: Sparse observations do not uniquely determine contacts or subsurface relationships.
tasks.human_edge: Draw a defensible interpretation and show where evidence is limited.

ambition.what: Prepare another checked geological output format from the same qualified interpretation.

tasks.altitude: Focus map work on geological meaning and uncertainty.

reach.task: Use the geological map or section
reach.learn: Distinguish measured observations from interpreted relationships.

evidence.claim: Native geological drawing presets and layouts could reduce drafting and output preparation, while geological interpretation remains human.

assumptions: OTHER means the geological mapping and drafting system. The task includes its notes and actual drawing work, not just a source lookup.

The technician produces source ID, coordinate reference, location, depth, units, observed attribute, scale and output scope in s3 with all 15 hours retained. Missing datum or depth references stop layout assembly and require manual resolution.
Native tools support the technician's drawing choices; they do not infer geological contacts. Layout population is a distinct draft action and final source checking retains five hours.
Native presets and layouts come first. No hidden publication or external send is proposed, and ordinary same-system saves have no author approval stage or separate saving.
unknowns: Layer compatibility, source coordinate quality and output metadata coverage.
research_questions: Does native drafting save time when source layers use incompatible coordinates or incomplete depth metadata?

already_counted.description: Capture coordinates, depth references and observation attributes.

incremental.description: Maintain drawing presets, source links and output layout checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=83, gross=17; upkeep=4 gives net=13. Conservative case: incompatible layers leave lookup at 15 hours, drafting at 26 and manual layout correction at four, with other work retaining 50; R=95, net=1. Compatible layers and output metadata give lookup 13, drawing 24 and layout one, R=88, net=8. Scope, input capture, interpretation and checking retain 50 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in geological field programmes and separately record and hand over observations.

steps.what: Retrieve the geological survey programme, field instructions and relevant site records
Travel to the survey, drilling or exploration location and obtain site access
Prepare and check the survey or logging equipment for the field activity
Participate in geological surveys, prospecting, drilling or well logging as assigned
Record field locations, readings, geological observations and encountered programme issues
Hand over the checked field record and unresolved issues to the programme scientist

tasks.design: Configure linked programme instructions and field record headings in {DOCS}. Retain travel, equipment preparation and actual field participation, separately record readings and observations, and hand over the checked record to the programme scientist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programme references and field observation headings are repeatedly assembled.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference views and field record templates can reduce lookup and writing.
tasks.still_hard: Field conditions, equipment behaviour and unexpected geological observations require practical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unreliable readings or conditions that require changing the field activity.
tasks.altitude: Improve field record completeness without delegating participation or judgement.

reach.learn: Check location, method and field limitations before drawing conclusions.

evidence.claim: Native programme reference views and field record headings could reduce supporting lookup and entry; the field participation saving is not assumed.

assumptions: This task includes the actual field record and scientist handover, separately priced from participation. Later cross-source compilation and map production are separate tasks, with no repeated capture saving.

The technician produces programme and location ID, time, method, reading, units, observation and limitation fields in s5, retaining 10.5 hours. Missing location or method context requires manual clarification, not invented metadata.
Native views and headings come first. No automated instrument operation, field decision or geological interpretation is proposed.
The actual colleague handover checks final record and recipient within its five retained hours. Ordinary author saves have no added approval stage or separate saving.
unknowns: Field conditions, offline record access and current location metadata quality.
research_questions: Can a native field template reduce writing when offline work and unusual observations require free text?

already_counted.description: Capture field observations and method context.

incremental.description: Maintain field record headings and programme links.

approvals.approved_version: Exact field record, unresolved issues and receiving programme scientist; changed content or recipient requires a fresh handover-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=93.5, gross=6.5; upkeep=1.5 gives net=5. Conservative case: offline or unfamiliar programmes retain all ten lookup hours and 13.5 of 15 record hours; R=98.5, net=0. A usable reference view and field layout retain nine lookup and 11.5 record hours, R=95.5, net=3. Travel, preparation, field participation and actual handover retain 75 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain sample and field judgement while improving complete source records, fixed calculations and geological outputs.
reach: Connect actual measurements with source-comparable datasets and qualified geological drawings.
skills_to_grow: Check drawing metadata and geological uncertainty
role.ambitious_version: A geological technician who performs careful practical work and supplies clear records, reliable datasets and defensible geological outputs.
